sanskrit.deva:
पुरमेकादशद्वारमजस्यावक्रचेतसः ।
अनुष्ठाय न शोचति विमुक्तश्च विमुच्यते ।
एतद्वै तत् ॥ १ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
puram ekādaśadvāram ajasyāvakracetasaḥ |
anuṣṭhāya na śocati vimuktaś ca vimucyate |
etad vai tat || 1 ||

lines.iast: puram ekādaśadvāram ajasyāvakracetasaḥ
lines.deva: पुरमेकादशद्वारमजस्यावक्रचेतसः

lines.iast: anuṣṭhāya na śocati vimuktaś ca vimucyate
lines.deva: अनुष्ठाय न शोचति विमुक्तश्च विमुच्यते

lines.iast: etad vai tat
lines.deva: एतद्वै तत्

padaccheda.iast: puram ekādaśa-dvāram ajasya a-vakra-cetasaḥ anuṣṭhāya na śocati vimuktaḥ ca vimucyate etat vai tat
padaccheda.deva: पुरम् एकादश-द्वारम् अजस्य अ-वक्र-चेतसः अनुष्ठाय न शोचति विमुक्तः च विमुच्यते एतत् वै तत्

grammar.en: past passive participle m. nom. sg.

translations.text: “There is a city of eleven gates, belonging to the unborn one whose consciousness never bends. Meditating on its lord, one does not grieve; and, already freed, one is set free. This indeed is that.”

notes: Śaṅkara: the city is the body, which like a city has gatekeepers, rulers and much equipment, and exists for a master who is no part of it. The eleven gates are the seven in the head, three below including the navel, and one at the crown. avakracetas: whose consciousness, like the light of the sun, is always the same. anuṣṭhāya: having meditated on the supreme Lord, the master of the city. ‘Freed’ here and now from the bonds of desire and action made by ignorance, he is ‘set free’: he takes no further body.

sanskrit.deva:
हंसः शुचिषद्वसुरन्तरिक्षसद्धोता वेदिषदतिथिर्दुरोणसत् ।
नृषद्वरसदृतसद्व्योमसदब्जा गोजा ऋतजा अद्रिजा ऋतं बृहत् ॥ २ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
haṃsaḥ śuciṣad vasur antarikṣasad dhotā vediṣad atithir duroṇasat |
nṛṣad varasad ṛtasad vyomasad abjā gojā ṛtajā adrijā ṛtaṃ bṛhat || 2 ||

lines.iast: haṃsaḥ śuciṣad vasur antarikṣasad dhotā vediṣad atithir duroṇasat
lines.deva: हंसः शुचिषद्वसुरन्तरिक्षसद्धोता वेदिषदतिथिर्दुरोणसत्

lines.iast: nṛṣad varasad ṛtasad vyomasad abjā gojā ṛtajā adrijā ṛtaṃ bṛhat
lines.deva: नृषद्वरसदृतसद्व्योमसदब्जा गोजा ऋतजा अद्रिजा ऋतं बृहत्

padaccheda.iast: haṃsaḥ śuciṣat vasuḥ antarikṣa-sat hotā vediṣat atithiḥ duroṇa-sat nṛṣat vara-sat ṛta-sat vyoma-sat ap-jāḥ go-jāḥ ṛta-jāḥ adri-jāḥ ṛtam bṛhat
padaccheda.deva: हंसः शुचिषत् वसुः अन्तरिक्ष-सत् होता वेदिषत् अतिथिः दुरोण-सत् नृषत् वर-सत् ऋत-सत् व्योम-सत् अप्-जाः गो-जाः ऋत-जाः अद्रि-जाः ऋतम् बृहत्

words.meaning: the one who gives all a dwelling (air)
dwelling in the jar, or in houses

translations.text: “He is the sun dwelling in the bright sky, the air dwelling in the mid-region, the fire dwelling on the altar of the earth, the guest dwelling in the house. He dwells in men, in the gods, in truth, in space. He is born in the waters, on the earth, in the sacrifice, from the mountains. He is the true, the great.”

notes: Śaṅkara: the Self dwells not in the city of one body only but in all. haṃsa, ‘the one who goes’: the sun; vasu, ‘he who gives all a dwelling’: air; hotṛ: fire; the altar is the earth. atithi: Soma in the jar, or a brahmin guest in houses. vara: the gods. abjā: as conch, pearl-oyster and sea creatures; gojā: as rice and barley; ṛtajā: as the parts of the sacrifice; adrijā: as rivers. Though the Self of all, it is ṛta, of unfailing nature, and great as the cause of all. The one all-pervading Self is the Self of the world: there is no division in it.

sanskrit.deva:
ऊर्ध्वं प्राणमुन्नयति अपानं प्रत्यगस्यति ।
मध्ये वामनमासीनं विश्वे देवा उपासते ॥ ३ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
ūrdhvaṃ prāṇam unnayati apānaṃ pratyag asyati |
madhye vāmanam āsīnaṃ viśve devā upāsate || 3 ||

lines.iast: ūrdhvaṃ prāṇam unnayati apānaṃ pratyag asyati
lines.deva: ऊर्ध्वं प्राणमुन्नयति अपानं प्रत्यगस्यति

lines.iast: madhye vāmanam āsīnaṃ viśve devā upāsate
lines.deva: मध्ये वामनमासीनं विश्वे देवा उपासते

padaccheda.iast: ūrdhvam prāṇam unnayati apānam pratyak asyati madhye vāmanam āsīnam viśve devāḥ upāsate
padaccheda.deva: ऊर्ध्वम् प्राणम् उन्नयति अपानम् प्रत्यक् अस्यति मध्ये वामनम् आसीनम् विश्वे देवाः उपासते

translations.text: “He leads the out-breath upward and casts the in-breath downward. Him, the adorable one seated in the middle, all the gods wait upon.”

notes: Śaṅkara: this gives a mark by which the Self may be known. ‘In the middle’: in the space of the lotus of the heart. vāmana: the one to be adored (vananīya). The gods are the eye and the other senses, which bring him the perceptions of form and the rest as subjects bring tribute to a king. He for whose sake all the workings of breath and senses go on is thereby shown to be other than they.

sanskrit.deva:
अस्य विस्रंसमानस्य शरीरस्थस्य देहिनः ।
देहाद्विमुच्यमानस्य किमत्र परिशिष्यते ।
एतद्वै तत् ॥ ४ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
asya visraṃsamānasya śarīrasthasya dehinaḥ |
dehād vimucyamānasya kim atra pariśiṣyate |
etad vai tat || 4 ||

lines.iast: asya visraṃsamānasya śarīrasthasya dehinaḥ
lines.deva: अस्य विस्रंसमानस्य शरीरस्थस्य देहिनः

lines.iast: dehād vimucyamānasya kim atra pariśiṣyate
lines.deva: देहाद्विमुच्यमानस्य किमत्र परिशिष्यते

lines.iast: etad vai tat
lines.deva: एतद्वै तत्

padaccheda.iast: asya visraṃsamānasya śarīra-sthasya dehinaḥ dehāt vimucyamānasya kim atra pariśiṣyate etat vai tat
padaccheda.deva: अस्य विस्रंसमानस्य शरीर-स्थस्य देहिनः देहात् विमुच्यमानस्य किम् अत्र परिशिष्यते एतत् वै तत्

translations.text: “When this embodied one who dwells in the body slips away and is released from the body, what remains here? This indeed is that.”

notes: Śaṅkara: nothing remains of the whole group of breaths and organs; all of it loses its strength in a moment, as the townspeople do when the master of the city has gone. That whose departure brings this about is the Self, shown to be other than they.

sanskrit.deva:
न प्राणेन नापानेन मर्त्यो जीवति कश्चन ।
इतरेण तु जीवन्ति यस्मिन्नेतावुपाश्रितौ ॥ ५ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
na prāṇena nāpānena martyo jīvati kaścana |
itareṇa tu jīvanti yasminn etāv upāśritau || 5 ||

lines.iast: na prāṇena nāpānena martyo jīvati kaścana
lines.deva: न प्राणेन नापानेन मर्त्यो जीवति कश्चन

lines.iast: itareṇa tu jīvanti yasminn etāv upāśritau
lines.deva: इतरेण तु जीवन्ति यस्मिन्नेतावुपाश्रितौ

padaccheda.iast: na prāṇena na apānena martyaḥ jīvati kaścana itareṇa tu jīvanti yasmin etau upāśritau
padaccheda.deva: न प्राणेन न अपानेन मर्त्यः जीवति कश्चन इतरेण तु जीवन्ति यस्मिन् एतौ उपाश्रितौ

grammar.en: past passive participle m. nom. du.

translations.text: “No mortal lives by the out-breath or by the in-breath. They live by another, on which these two depend.”

notes: Śaṅkara: things that work together in combination exist for the sake of something else, as a house does; so the breaths cannot themselves be the cause of life. All live by that which is other than the combination, the Self.

sanskrit.deva:
हन्त त इदं प्रवक्ष्यामि गुह्यं ब्रह्म सनातनम् ।
यथा च मरणं प्राप्य आत्मा भवति गौतम ॥ ६ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
hanta ta idaṃ pravakṣyāmi guhyaṃ brahma sanātanam |
yathā ca maraṇaṃ prāpya ātmā bhavati gautama || 6 ||

lines.iast: hanta ta idaṃ pravakṣyāmi guhyaṃ brahma sanātanam
lines.deva: हन्त त इदं प्रवक्ष्यामि गुह्यं ब्रह्म सनातनम्

lines.iast: yathā ca maraṇaṃ prāpya ātmā bhavati gautama
lines.deva: यथा च मरणं प्राप्य आत्मा भवति गौतम

padaccheda.iast: hanta te idam pravakṣyāmi guhyam brahma sanātanam yathā ca maraṇam prāpya ātmā bhavati gautama
padaccheda.deva: हन्त ते इदम् प्रवक्ष्यामि गुह्यम् ब्रह्म सनातनम् यथा च मरणम् प्राप्य आत्मा भवति गौतम

translations.text: “Come, I shall declare to you this secret, eternal Brahman, and also how the self fares on meeting death, O Gautama.”

notes: Śaṅkara: by knowing it the whole cycle of birth and death comes to an end; and hear how the self of one who does not know it passes on after death.

sanskrit.deva:
योनिमन्ये प्रपद्यन्ते शरीरत्वाय देहिनः ।
स्थाणुमन्येऽनुसंयन्ति यथाकर्म यथाश्रुतम् ॥ ७ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
yonim anye prapadyante śarīratvāya dehinaḥ |
sthāṇum anye 'nusaṃyanti yathākarma yathāśrutam || 7 ||

lines.iast: yonim anye prapadyante śarīratvāya dehinaḥ
lines.deva: योनिमन्ये प्रपद्यन्ते शरीरत्वाय देहिनः

lines.iast: sthāṇum anye 'nusaṃyanti yathākarma yathāśrutam
lines.deva: स्थाणुमन्येऽनुसंयन्ति यथाकर्म यथाश्रुतम्

padaccheda.iast: yonim anye prapadyante śarīra-tvāya dehinaḥ sthāṇum anye anusaṃyanti yathākarma yathāśrutam
padaccheda.deva: योनिम् अन्ये प्रपद्यन्ते शरीर-त्वाय देहिनः स्थाणुम् अन्ये अनुसंयन्ति यथाकर्म यथाश्रुतम्

translations.text: “Some embodied ones enter a womb to take a body; others pass into the motionless state of plants: each according to his action, each according to his knowledge.”

notes: Śaṅkara: these are the ignorant. sthāṇu: the state of trees and other unmoving things, to which the very lowest go. Each takes a body in keeping with the action done in this life and the knowledge gained.

sanskrit.deva:
य एष सुप्तेषु जागर्ति कामं कामं पुरुषो निर्मिमाणः ।
तदेव शुक्रं तद्ब्रह्म तदेवामृतमुच्यते ।
तस्मिंल्लोकाः श्रिताः सर्वे तदु नात्येति कश्चन ।
एतद्वै तत् ॥ ८ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
ya eṣa supteṣu jāgarti kāmaṃ kāmaṃ puruṣo nirmimāṇaḥ |
tad eva śukraṃ tad brahma tad evāmṛtam ucyate |
tasmiṃl lokāḥ śritāḥ sarve tad u nātyeti kaścana |
etad vai tat || 8 ||

lines.iast: ya eṣa supteṣu jāgarti kāmaṃ kāmaṃ puruṣo nirmimāṇaḥ
lines.deva: य एष सुप्तेषु जागर्ति कामं कामं पुरुषो निर्मिमाणः

lines.iast: tad eva śukraṃ tad brahma tad evāmṛtam ucyate
lines.deva: तदेव शुक्रं तद्ब्रह्म तदेवामृतमुच्यते

lines.iast: tasmiṃl lokāḥ śritāḥ sarve tad u nātyeti kaścana
lines.deva: तस्मिंल्लोकाः श्रिताः सर्वे तदु नात्येति कश्चन

lines.iast: etad vai tat
lines.deva: एतद्वै तत्

padaccheda.iast: yaḥ eṣaḥ supteṣu jāgarti kāmam kāmam puruṣaḥ nirmimāṇaḥ tat eva śukram tat brahma tat eva amṛtam ucyate tasmin lokāḥ śritāḥ sarve tat u na atyeti kaścana etat vai tat
padaccheda.deva: यः एषः सुप्तेषु जागर्ति कामम् कामम् पुरुषः निर्मिमाणः तत् एव शुक्रम् तत् ब्रह्म तत् एव अमृतम् उच्यते तस्मिन् लोकाः श्रिताः सर्वे तत् उ न अत्येति कश्चन एतत् वै तत्

grammar.en: past passive participle m. loc. pl.
past passive participle m. nom. pl.

translations.text: “The Person who stays awake while they sleep, shaping desire after desire: that alone is the pure, that is Brahman, that alone is called the immortal. In it all the worlds rest, and no one goes beyond it. This indeed is that.”

notes: Śaṅkara: this is the secret Brahman that was promised. ‘They’ are the breaths and the senses. Out of ignorance he brings forth one desired object after another. There is no other secret Brahman than this.

sanskrit.deva:
अग्निर्यथैको भुवनं प्रविष्टो रूपं रूपं प्रतिरूपो बभूव ।
एकस्तथा सर्वभूतान्तरात्मा रूपं रूपं प्रतिरूपो बहिश्च ॥ ९ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
agnir yathaiko bhuvanaṃ praviṣṭo rūpaṃ rūpaṃ pratirūpo babhūva |
ekas tathā sarvabhūtāntarātmā rūpaṃ rūpaṃ pratirūpo bahiś ca || 9 ||

lines.iast: agnir yathaiko bhuvanaṃ praviṣṭo rūpaṃ rūpaṃ pratirūpo babhūva
lines.deva: अग्निर्यथैको भुवनं प्रविष्टो रूपं रूपं प्रतिरूपो बभूव

lines.iast: ekas tathā sarvabhūtāntarātmā rūpaṃ rūpaṃ pratirūpo bahiś ca
lines.deva: एकस्तथा सर्वभूतान्तरात्मा रूपं रूपं प्रतिरूपो बहिश्च

padaccheda.iast: agniḥ yathā ekaḥ bhuvanam praviṣṭaḥ rūpam rūpam pratirūpaḥ babhūva ekaḥ tathā sarva-bhūta-antarātmā rūpam rūpam pratirūpaḥ bahiḥ ca
padaccheda.deva: अग्निः यथा एकः भुवनम् प्रविष्टः रूपम् रूपम् प्रतिरूपः बभूव एकः तथा सर्व-भूत-अन्तरात्मा रूपम् रूपम् प्रतिरूपः बहिः च

grammar.en: past passive participle m. nom. sg.

words.meaning: the inner Self of all beings

translations.text: “As the one fire, having entered the world, takes a form to match each form it meets, so the one inner Self of all beings takes a form to match each form; and it is outside them too.”

notes: Śaṅkara: the Upaniṣad says this again and again, since minds unsettled by the arguments of many disputants do not take in the oneness of the Self. Fire takes the shape of whatever it burns, wood and the like. ‘Outside’: in its own unchanged nature, like space.

sanskrit.deva:
वायुर्यथैको भुवनं प्रविष्टो रूपं रूपं प्रतिरूपो बभूव ।
एकस्तथा सर्वभूतान्तरात्मा रूपं रूपं प्रतिरूपो बहिश्च ॥ १० ॥
sanskrit.iast:
vāyur yathaiko bhuvanaṃ praviṣṭo rūpaṃ rūpaṃ pratirūpo babhūva |
ekas tathā sarvabhūtāntarātmā rūpaṃ rūpaṃ pratirūpo bahiś ca || 10 ||

lines.iast: vāyur yathaiko bhuvanaṃ praviṣṭo rūpaṃ rūpaṃ pratirūpo babhūva
lines.deva: वायुर्यथैको भुवनं प्रविष्टो रूपं रूपं प्रतिरूपो बभूव

lines.iast: ekas tathā sarvabhūtāntarātmā rūpaṃ rūpaṃ pratirūpo bahiś ca
lines.deva: एकस्तथा सर्वभूतान्तरात्मा रूपं रूपं प्रतिरूपो बहिश्च

padaccheda.iast: vāyuḥ yathā ekaḥ bhuvanam praviṣṭaḥ rūpam rūpam pratirūpaḥ babhūva ekaḥ tathā sarva-bhūta-antarātmā rūpam rūpam pratirūpaḥ bahiḥ ca
padaccheda.deva: वायुः यथा एकः भुवनम् प्रविष्टः रूपम् रूपम् प्रतिरूपः बभूव एकः तथा सर्व-भूत-अन्तरात्मा रूपम् रूपम् प्रतिरूपः बहिः च

grammar.en: past passive participle m. nom. sg.

words.meaning: the inner Self of all beings

translations.text: “As the one air, having entered the world, takes a form to match each form it meets, so the one inner Self of all beings takes a form to match each form; and it is outside them too.”

notes: Śaṅkara: a second illustration: air enters bodies as the life-breath.

sanskrit.deva:
सूर्यो यथा सर्वलोकस्य चक्षुर्न लिप्यते चाक्षुषैर्बाह्यदोषैः ।
एकस्तथा सर्वभूतान्तरात्मा न लिप्यते लोकदुःखेन बाह्यः ॥ ११ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
sūryo yathā sarvalokasya cakṣur na lipyate cākṣuṣair bāhyadoṣaiḥ |
ekas tathā sarvabhūtāntarātmā na lipyate lokaduḥkhena bāhyaḥ || 11 ||

lines.iast: sūryo yathā sarvalokasya cakṣur na lipyate cākṣuṣair bāhyadoṣaiḥ
lines.deva: सूर्यो यथा सर्वलोकस्य चक्षुर्न लिप्यते चाक्षुषैर्बाह्यदोषैः

lines.iast: ekas tathā sarvabhūtāntarātmā na lipyate lokaduḥkhena bāhyaḥ
lines.deva: एकस्तथा सर्वभूतान्तरात्मा न लिप्यते लोकदुःखेन बाह्यः

padaccheda.iast: sūryaḥ yathā sarva-lokasya cakṣuḥ na lipyate cākṣuṣaiḥ bāhya-doṣaiḥ ekaḥ tathā sarva-bhūta-antarātmā na lipyate loka-duḥkhena bāhyaḥ
padaccheda.deva: सूर्यः यथा सर्व-लोकस्य चक्षुः न लिप्यते चाक्षुषैः बाह्य-दोषैः एकः तथा सर्व-भूत-अन्तरात्मा न लिप्यते लोक-दुःखेन बाह्यः

words.meaning: the inner Self of all beings
by the sorrow of the world

translations.text: “As the sun, the eye of the whole world, is not stained by the outward faults that the eye sees, so the one inner Self of all beings is not stained by the sorrow of the world, for it stands outside it.”

notes: Śaṅkara: this answers the objection that, if the one Self is the Self of all, the sorrow of worldly life must belong to the supreme itself. The sun lights up unclean things and is untouched by them. People suffer through ignorance laid upon the Self; that ignorance is not truly in it, just as the snake is not in the rope nor silver in mother-of-pearl.

sanskrit.deva:
एको वशी सर्वभूतान्तरात्मा एकं रूपं बहुधा यः करोति ।
तमात्मस्थं येऽनुपश्यन्ति धीरास्तेषां सुखं शाश्वतं नेतरेषाम् ॥ १२ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
eko vaśī sarvabhūtāntarātmā ekaṃ rūpaṃ bahudhā yaḥ karoti |
tam ātmasthaṃ ye 'nupaśyanti dhīrās teṣāṃ sukhaṃ śāśvataṃ netareṣām || 12 ||

lines.iast: eko vaśī sarvabhūtāntarātmā ekaṃ rūpaṃ bahudhā yaḥ karoti
lines.deva: एको वशी सर्वभूतान्तरात्मा एकं रूपं बहुधा यः करोति

lines.iast: tam ātmasthaṃ ye 'nupaśyanti dhīrās teṣāṃ sukhaṃ śāśvataṃ netareṣām
lines.deva: तमात्मस्थं येऽनुपश्यन्ति धीरास्तेषां सुखं शाश्वतं नेतरेषाम्

padaccheda.iast: ekaḥ vaśī sarva-bhūta-antarātmā ekam rūpam bahudhā yaḥ karoti tam ātma-stham ye anupaśyanti dhīrāḥ teṣām sukham śāśvatam na itareṣām
padaccheda.deva: एकः वशी सर्व-भूत-अन्तरात्मा एकम् रूपम् बहुधा यः करोति तम् आत्म-स्थम् ये अनुपश्यन्ति धीराः तेषाम् सुखम् शाश्वतम् न इतरेषाम्

words.meaning: the inner Self of all beings

translations.text: “The one ruler, the inner Self of all beings, who makes his one form manifold: the wise who perceive him dwelling in themselves have everlasting happiness, and no others.”

notes: Śaṅkara: he is the supreme Lord, free, with none equal or greater; the whole world is under his sway. By his mere being, through powers beyond thought, he makes the one pure consciousness many through the limiting adjuncts of name and form. ātmastha: shown as consciousness in the intellect, in the space of the heart; the body is not really his container, any more than a mirror contains the face. anu: after the teaching of teacher and scripture. The happiness is the bliss of the Self.

sanskrit.deva:
नित्योऽनित्यानां चेतनश्चेतनानामेको बहूनां यो विदधाति कामान् ।
तमात्मस्थं येऽनुपश्यन्ति धीरास्तेषां शान्तिः शाश्वती नेतरेषाम् ॥ १३ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
nityo 'nityānāṃ cetanaś cetanānām eko bahūnāṃ yo vidadhāti kāmān |
tam ātmasthaṃ ye 'nupaśyanti dhīrās teṣāṃ śāntiḥ śāśvatī netareṣām || 13 ||

lines.iast: nityo 'nityānāṃ cetanaś cetanānām eko bahūnāṃ yo vidadhāti kāmān
lines.deva: नित्योऽनित्यानां चेतनश्चेतनानामेको बहूनां यो विदधाति कामान्

lines.iast: tam ātmasthaṃ ye 'nupaśyanti dhīrās teṣāṃ śāntiḥ śāśvatī netareṣām
lines.deva: तमात्मस्थं येऽनुपश्यन्ति धीरास्तेषां शान्तिः शाश्वती नेतरेषाम्

padaccheda.iast: nityaḥ anityānām cetanaḥ cetanānām ekaḥ bahūnām yaḥ vidadhāti kāmān tam ātma-stham ye anupaśyanti dhīrāḥ teṣām śāntiḥ śāśvatī na itareṣām
padaccheda.deva: नित्यः अनित्यानाम् चेतनः चेतनानाम् एकः बहूनाम् यः विदधाति कामान् तम् आत्म-स्थम् ये अनुपश्यन्ति धीराः तेषाम् शान्तिः शाश्वती न इतरेषाम्

translations.text: “The eternal among the non-eternal, the conscious among the conscious, the one who grants the desires of the many: the wise who perceive him dwelling in themselves have everlasting peace, and no others.”

notes: Śaṅkara: other beings, from Brahmā down, are conscious only through the consciousness of the Self, as water burns only through fire. All-knowing and Lord of all, he gives those who desire the fruits of their actions, each according to his action. The peace is cessation, and it is their very Self.

sanskrit.deva:
तदेतदिति मन्यन्तेऽनिर्देश्यं परमं सुखम् ।
कथं नु तद्विजानीयां किमु भाति विभाति वा ॥ १४ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
tad etad iti manyante 'nirdeśyaṃ paramaṃ sukham |
kathaṃ nu tad vijānīyāṃ kim u bhāti vibhāti vā || 14 ||

lines.iast: tad etad iti manyante 'nirdeśyaṃ paramaṃ sukham
lines.deva: तदेतदिति मन्यन्तेऽनिर्देश्यं परमं सुखम्

lines.iast: kathaṃ nu tad vijānīyāṃ kim u bhāti vibhāti vā
lines.deva: कथं नु तद्विजानीयां किमु भाति विभाति वा

padaccheda.iast: tat etat iti manyante a-nirdeśyam paramam sukham katham nu tat vijānīyām kim u bhāti vibhāti vā
padaccheda.deva: तत् एतत् इति मन्यन्ते अ-निर्देश्यम् परमम् सुखम् कथम् नु तत् विजानीयाम् किम् उ भाति विभाति वा

translations.text: “‘That is this’: so they hold the indescribable, supreme happiness to be. How, then, may I know it? Does it shine of itself, and is it clearly seen, or not?”

notes: Śaṅkara: the happiness of knowing the Self cannot be pointed out and lies beyond the speech and mind of ordinary men; yet those who have laid down all desires hold it to be directly present, ‘this’. The question is how one may make it an object of one's own understanding as they do: is it luminous, so that it is plainly seen by our understanding, or not?

sanskrit.deva:
न तत्र सूर्यो भाति न चन्द्रतारकं नेमा विद्युतो भान्ति कुतोऽयमग्निः ।
तमेव भान्तमनु भाति सर्वं तस्य भासा सर्वमिदं विभाति ॥ १५ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
na tatra sūryo bhāti na candratārakaṃ nemā vidyuto bhānti kuto 'yam agniḥ |
tam eva bhāntam anu bhāti sarvaṃ tasya bhāsā sarvam idaṃ vibhāti || 15 ||

lines.iast: na tatra sūryo bhāti na candratārakaṃ nemā vidyuto bhānti kuto 'yam agniḥ
lines.deva: न तत्र सूर्यो भाति न चन्द्रतारकं नेमा विद्युतो भान्ति कुतोऽयमग्निः

lines.iast: tam eva bhāntam anu bhāti sarvaṃ tasya bhāsā sarvam idaṃ vibhāti
lines.deva: तमेव भान्तमनु भाति सर्वं तस्य भासा सर्वमिदं विभाति

padaccheda.iast: na tatra sūryaḥ bhāti na candra-tārakam na imāḥ vidyutaḥ bhānti kutaḥ ayam agniḥ tam eva bhāntam anu bhāti sarvam tasya bhāsā sarvam idam vibhāti
padaccheda.deva: न तत्र सूर्यः भाति न चन्द्र-तारकम् न इमाः विद्युतः भान्ति कुतः अयम् अग्निः तम् एव भान्तम् अनु भाति सर्वम् तस्य भासा सर्वम् इदम् विभाति

translations.text: “There the sun does not shine, nor the moon and stars, nor do these lightnings shine; how then this fire? Everything shines only after him, as he shines; by his light all this shines.”

notes: Śaṅkara: this is the answer: it both shines and is clearly seen. The sun, which lights up everything, does not light up Brahman, one's own Self. All else shines after it, as water or a firebrand burns only through contact with fire and not of itself. From the varied light found in its effects, the luminous nature of Brahman is known to be its own.
